title: Post-demo notes: observability & ops interop vs hyperscalers — clarifications and next tests
text:
Post-demo notes: observability & ops interop vs hyperscalers — clarifications and next tests

["From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@datawave.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-demo notes: observability & ops interop vs hyperscalers — clarifications and next tests

Priya / DataWave team,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the candid tradeoffs you called out vs the hyperscaler offerings. Quick recap of the things we discussed and proposed next tests so the CS/infra teams can compare apples-to-apples:

Summary of competitive points mentioned on the call:
- Hyperscaler A (Vertex/etc): good for managed endpoints but limited KV/prefix caching and per-token unit economics at scale.
- Hyperscaler B (Bedrock/etc): strong model catalog but limited continuous-batching controls and less visibility into per-token compute breakdowns.
- Redwood differentiators we highlighted: runtime-level KV/prefix caching, configurable batching policies by route, and our per-route token + kernel-level telemetry in the Console (latency, GPU utilization, batch size distribution).

Requested clarifications you raised:
- Telemetry formats: you want OpenTelemetry traces and a Splunk-compatible JSON export for traces/logs.
- Retention & access: 90-day raw trace retention is your current requirement; longer-term aggregated metrics are OK to store in your analytics.
- Security/compliance: you asked whether audit logs and request metadata are available for Private deployments (they are — we can provide event-level exports).

Proposed next tests (what Redwood will deliver / what DataWave should run):
1) Ops interop smoke: push 1k synthetic demo requests with 3 prompt templates to validate P95 under 120ms and end-to-end spans propagated to Splunk.
2) Batch/throughput play: 5-minute sustained load to measure batching behavior and tokens/sec.
3) KV/prefix caching validation: run session warmup, then cold vs warm token cost comparison.

Attachments: proposed-MAP.xlsx (high-level mutual action plan), telemetry-specs.pdf (sample OTEL/JSON export schema).

Next steps / asks:
- Priya: can your infra/security team confirm whether Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) endpoints are available for a short-term test?
- Sergio / Ben: we need to prepare the quickstart scripts and perf harness for the 1k-run; I can share a lightweight Redwood quickstart repo and a list of three canonical prompts.
- DataWave: grant a short-lived test key or let us run against your staging VPC endpoint (whichever you prefer).

I'll follow up with an internal assignment email. Thanks — looking forward to the tests.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0173

--
Attachments: proposed-MAP.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB), telemetry-specs.pdf (PDF, 128KB)
", "From: Priya Rao <priya@datawave.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: DataWave Security <security@datawave.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes: observability & ops interop vs hyperscalers — clarifications and next tests

Thanks, Vanessa — and thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side so we can scope the tests properly:

1) Splunk: we can expose a short-lived HEC token for staging. Will confirm by EOD tomorrow but that’s likely fine.
2) Retention: 90 days for raw traces is our baseline; if you can show how aggregated metrics can be exported to our long-term analytics that would be ideal.
3) Data sensitivity: can you confirm whether request payloads can be redacted at the agent/export level before being forwarded to Splunk? We need to avoid PII in logs.

Also, on the competitive side, our infra lead asked whether Redwood's Console can surface per-model kernel selection (i.e., the model+kernel pair used per request) so we can audit performance regressions when you recommend quantized variants. Is that included in the telemetry-specs.pdf?

If you can answer the above and share the quickstart scripts, we’ll kick off the 1k-run next week.

Regards,
Priya Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, DataWave Solutions
priya@datawave.ai

Looping in Ben with the test plan and task assignments. Short plan below so we have internal clarity: 

- Ben: own the perf harness (locust-based) and run the 1k synthetic requests against DataWave staging. Confirm p95 target and share raw trace exports.
- Vanessa: share quickstart scripts, three prompt templates, and the MAP spreadsheet with explicit timelines.
- Sergio (me): produce an ops-interop-checklist.md that details OTEL keys, JSON field names we export, and how to redact request text at export time. I’ll attach that doc to HubSpot and link in the test artifacts.

About the kernel/model telemetry question: yes, our Console includes a per-request field we call kernel_id which maps to the kernel selection (model variant + quantization profile). I’ll add a small note to telemetry-specs.pdf with the exact field name and values your infra team can map.

Tentative timeline: share quickstart + scripts by Mon, 2 Nov; run tests Tue-Wed; deliver results by Thu, 5 Nov. If DataWave needs earlier, we can compress.

Ben — can you confirm availability to run the harness on Tue morning PST?

Thanks,
Sergio
